newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signs motherhood health bill.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signs motherhood health bill.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday signed into law a bill that requires health insurers to allow new mothers to stay in the hospital at least 48 hours after childbirth.

"Parents may rush to the hospital, but they shouldn't be rushed out of it unless it's the right thing to do for the parent and the child," Clinton said of the measure, which grew from complaints about health care plans that forced new mothers to leave the hospital as soon as 10 hours after a normal delivery.

The "Newborns' and Mothers' Protection Act" was tied to a $64.4 billion government money bill that also improves health benefits for mental patients and children with spina bifida born to Vietnam veterans.

It was approved by a Republican-controlled Congress that is increasingly putting its own interests above those of the party's trouble-plagued presidential candidate Bob Dole. "We did not want to be branded as against 48 hours and therefore it passed," a House Republican aide said.

"By ensuring 48-hour hospital stays for mothers and newborns, battling discrimination against mental illness, caring for children of veterans who suffer from a terrible disease, we affirm that we will do everything we can to strengthen our families and build a stronger future," Clinton said.
